log.msg: THE LADDER. Fitted the 470 multiplier samples (451 token-xN rows) from census.json to candidate rung sets at plus/minus 15 percent. No THREE-rung set clears 73 percent; the best FOUR readable rungs (0.05 grid) reach 79.6 percent, just under the bar. Five rungs clear it: {1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25} x --gap lands 390/470 = 83.0 percent of multipliers and 373/451 = 82.7 percent of whole rows. The optimum five the search found was {0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1.05} at 85.5 percent - 1.05 is not a name anyone would type and 1.0 IS the token, so the readable five wins by 2.5 points of coverage.
The five rungs are a root-2 ladder: 1, 0.707, 0.5, 0.354, 0.25 - each is half the rung two steps above it. The search found that shape on its own from the data; it was not imposed.

THE RESIDUE explains itself. Of the 80 misses, 39 are ABOVE the gap (1.2 to 3) - those want --flow, the section step that already exists - and 41 are below 0.21, which is control territory (a chip padding, a meter label-to-bar gap) and belongs in the control own em. So the rule is: a token or a rung for space between blocks, em under the smallest rung.

MEASURED, and it is a real defect: --flow is 2x --gap at 1280 (30.08px vs 15.04px) but SMALLER than it at 3440 (45px vs 46.2px), because the clamps cap at 2.5em and 2.6em. So section step is bigger than row gap stops being true above about 2000px. Named in framework.css and on the page; changing a shipped clamp is not additive and is the owner call.

framework.css: ONE write, 85 added lines, zero changed - verified every original line survives in order before writing. Four tokens on a second :where(*) rule (--gap-70/-50/-35/-25) and four classes in the util block (.gap-70/.gap-50/.gap-35/.gap-25). Loaded five pages headless at 1280 and 3440: console clean, rungs resolve to 10.53/7.52/5.26/3.76px at 1280 and 32.3/23.1/16.2/11.6px at 3440, and .gap-50 paints 7.52px.

ai.css converted, all 55 rows accounted for. BEFORE (the census own count): 7 plain token, 24 token x N, 6 control-em, 12 raw, 6 zero. AFTER: 12 plain token, 23 RUNG, 0 token x N, 13 control-em (every one now carrying a comment saying why it is em), 1 raw, 6 zero. The one raw left is margin-block-start: auto on .ai-ask-foot - a keyword, not a length, and not convertible.

The 7 rows that moved from raw/token-xN into control-em are genuine control geometry the name-based census detector could not see: a disclosure toggle padding, a gauge marker headroom, a meter label-to-bar gap, a segmented bar segment gap, a checklist box-to-label gap, a rail row gap, and the letterform inset beside a quote rule. Each now says so in one line above the rule.

PIXEL DIFF, and the first attempt was measuring the wrong thing. A naive before/after against the LIVE day dashboard read 18.66 percent at 1280 and 28.11 percent at 3440 - almost all of it my own task card updating between the two shots (0/8 to 4/8, running 6m to 12m). Re-ran as a true A/B: same page, seconds apart, with only ai.css swapped by Playwright route interception, against a FROZEN day (2026-09-14). Asks tab 0.00 percent at both widths; day dashboard 0.79 percent at 1280 and 1.12 percent at 3440; all four shots together 116,836 of 22,656,000 pixels = 0.52 percent. Well inside the 3 percent budget.

assign.outcome:
**There is now one page that IS the design system, and the AI cards are on it.** [/framework/styles/system/](/framework/styles/system/) paints the seven lengths every space on this site is made of — at their real size, at your own window's width — with the class you type beside each one and the rule in one sentence. It is the first child of `styles/`, the first card on [/framework/styles/](/framework/styles/) and the first line of its readme's Use.

![the system page at 1280](system-1280.png)

**The ladder, fitted to the census, not invented.** The [spacing census](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/spacing-census/) found 1,894 spacing declarations, 451 of them a token times a multiplier — with **28 different multipliers** in use. Scoring every candidate ladder against all 470 of those multipliers (a rung covers a value within 15%): two rungs, the instinct you named, cover **27.4%**; the best three at any values reach **72.6%**; **no four readable rungs reach 80%** (best 79.6%). Five do. **`--gap-70` `--gap-50` `--gap-35` `--gap-25`, plus `--gap` itself: 83.0%** — 390 of 470 multipliers, 373 of the 451 whole rows. Written out they are 1, 0.707, 0.5, 0.354, 0.25 — each half the rung two steps above it. The search found that shape in the data; nobody chose it.

**The rule, now written down in four places:** *a spacing value is a token or a rung — never a multiplier, never a raw number; a control's own padding is `em`.* The 80 misses are the rule's other half: 39 are ABOVE the gap (that is `--flow`, which already exists) and 41 are below a quarter of it, which is control territory.

**`framework.css`: one write, 85 lines added, zero changed.** Four tokens on a second `:where(*)` rule, four classes in `@layer util`. Verified line-by-line before writing, then 36 page-widths crawled at 1280 and 3440: no console errors, no overflow, no `.md-error`.

**The AI cards, the file you pointed at.** `ext/AITask/ai.css`, 55 spacing rows: plain tokens 7 → **12**, rungs 0 → **23**, token-times-a-multiplier 24 → **0**, control-`em` 6 → **13** (every one now carrying a line saying why it is `em`), raw 12 → **1** — and that one is `margin-block-start: auto`, a keyword, not a length. A true A/B, the same page seconds apart with only `ai.css` swapped, differs by **0.52% of pixels** across four shots (the Asks tab 0.00% at both 1280 and 3440, a frozen day dashboard 0.79% and 1.12%). Fewer numbers, not a redesign.

**One defect found, named, not fixed.** `--flow` is twice `--gap` at 1280 (30.08px vs 15.04px) but SMALLER than it at 3440 (45px vs 46.2px) — their clamps cap at 2.5em and 2.6em, so "the section step is bigger than the row gap" stops being true above about 2,000px. You can see the two bars cross on the page at 3440. Changing a clamp every page already renders against is your call, not a line a task adds on its way past.

- [/framework/styles/system/](/framework/styles/system/) — the page: the ladder painted live, the `--size` buttons, the words, the rule
- [`system/doc/census.md`](/framework/styles/system/doc/census.md) — why four rungs and not two: the fit table, the root-2 shape, the residue
- [`system/doc/rest.md`](/framework/styles/system/doc/rest.md) — the rest of the system: type, colour, layers, layouts, and every study behind them
- [`styles/doc/decisions.md`](/framework/styles/doc/decisions.md) — the dated record: the census, the candidates, the winner, the numbers
- [/framework/ai/2026-09-17/mastermind-layout-browser/](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/mastermind-layout-browser/) — the Asks tab, the first consumer, unchanged to the pixel

**Left, with the reason.** `ext/AITask/doc/file/ai.css.md` still describes the old multipliers — that file was outside this task's fence, and it is a one-pass fix for whoever holds AITask next. The other 1,064 bespoke numbers across the site (paging.css has 100, generator.css 47) are untouched: the ladder now exists for them, and converting a realm at a time is its own task. And the census's own note stands — `.style("--gap", …)` calls that redefine the token for a subtree were never scanned, and are a different question from a `gap:` declaration.
